title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A sorted ascending array of distinct values was rotated at an unknown pivot. Given `nums`, return the minimum element. Values are unique.

predict_steps.prompt: If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is in which half?
predict_steps.hint: Rotation cut is to the right of mid.

viva.question: Why can you find the minimum in a rotated sorted array in logarithmic time?
expected_points: comparing mid to the right end reveals which half is unsorted
the minimum lives in the unsorted half
each step halves the remaining index range
distinct values keep the comparisons unambiguous

viva.question: What breaks if the array was never rotated and you still force a rightward move?
expected_points: an unrotated array is already sorted
mid is never greater than right so the search shrinks rightward correctly
jumping left to mid+1 would skip the true minimum at the front

viva.question: Why does nums[mid] greater than nums[right] mean the minimum is to the right of mid?
expected_points: the rotation cut lies in the right segment
the left segment through mid is an increasing run of large values
discarding mid and everything left of it is safe
the minimum cannot sit in that ascending left run
